key_insight: Neural networks trained on experimental quantum data from approximate ground states can predict unseen observables of a large 2D Heisenberg XXZ system, even near the phase boundary.
engineering_relevance: This shows a practical route for using quantum processors as data sources to learn many-body physics beyond the reach of exact classical simulation.
method: Generate quantum experiment data from approximate ground states of the 2D Heisenberg XXZ model.
Train neural networks on single-site expectation values, two-point correlations, and 12-body loop correlations.
Test predictions on unseen Hamiltonian parameters within the training region and in an out-of-distribution regime.
evidence_signal: The paper reports accurate prediction of spatially resolved observables using datasets from systems as large as 115 qubits, including evaluation both within distribution and near the phase boundary.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality of experimentally prepared approximate ground states, so noise and state-preparation errors may limit transfer to harder regimes.
paper_title: Learning ground state observables from quantum computing experiments
